note: The photographic brief. tools/tourism/prompting.py compiles this plus one country entry into a generation instruction; nothing here is model-specific except `model`. Edit this file to change how every generated image looks — no code change.
look: Documentary travel photography, shot on a full-frame camera in available light.
Believable colour: the greens are the greens of that place, not a preset.
Natural contrast with detail held in both the highlights and the shadows.
Sharp where the subject is, with the depth of field a real lens at this distance would give.
people: Anyone in frame is doing something, not posing for a camera.
Photograph people as individuals with their own business to attend to, at a respectful distance, in the clothes they would actually be wearing to do it.
No staged smiles at the lens, no visitor-and-local tableau, no one arranged as scenery.
avoid: any text, lettering, captions, titles, watermarks, signatures or logos anywhere in the frame
collage, split-screen, montage, multiple panels, borders, frames or vignettes
map shapes, continent outlines, flags or travel-poster layouts
HDR, heavy vignetting, orange-and-teal grading, crushed blacks, oversaturation
obvious stock-photo staging, or a composition with a hole left in it for type
$comment_direction: One line per category: what the photograph is actually of, and what would make it a good one rather than a generic one. This is the part worth editing.

direction.hero: The single establishing frame for the whole country — the landform or skyline it is known for, at the hour it looks most like itself. Wide, deep, and calm enough to carry a headline over.
direction.nature: A landscape read as terrain rather than as scenery: the shape of the ground, the way the vegetation changes with height, weather doing something.
direction.wildlife: One animal or a small group, in its own habitat, at a distance a real photographer would have kept. Behaviour, not a portrait.
direction.safari: A game drive as it actually looks — an open vehicle, dust, long light, guides working. The animals may be far off; that is the truth of it.
direction.mountains: Relief and scale: ridgelines receding, a route legible across the slope, cloud sitting where cloud sits on that massif.
direction.waterfalls: Moving water with the rock it falls over and the forest it falls through, at a shutter speed that keeps texture in the water rather than turning it to smoke.
direction.lakes-rivers: Water as a working part of the landscape — a shoreline, a crossing, a boat that belongs to someone.
direction.beaches: The specific coast, not a generic tropical beach: the real sand colour, the real vegetation behind it, the fishing boats and people who use it.
direction.forests: Inside the canopy rather than above it — light coming down in shafts, understorey, the density and the scale of the trunks.
direction.adventure: Effort in progress. Someone mid-activity with the terrain that makes it hard, equipment that has been used before.
direction.culture: A cultural practice being performed for the people it belongs to, in its own setting.
direction.traditional-people: A person or small group in traditional dress, photographed as individuals engaged in something, in their own surroundings and at their own eye level.
direction.food: Food as it is actually eaten and sold — a cooking fire, a market stall, a plate on a real table — not a styled overhead flat lay.
direction.festivals: A crowd and a moment inside it: movement, colour, the thing everyone is watching.
direction.crafts: Hands and tools at the point of work, with the material and the workshop around them.
direction.historic-sites: A built site with its age visible, given a sense of scale by the ground it stands on.
direction.heritage: An inherited object, building or practice still in use, in the setting that gives it meaning.
direction.cities: A working city: streets in use, real traffic, the mixture of buildings a city actually has, at a time of day with people in it.
direction.architecture: One building or a coherent group, read for its structure — the material, the rhythm of the openings, the light raking across it.
direction.local-life: An ordinary hour in an ordinary place. Nothing staged, nothing picturesque for its own sake.
direction.family-community: People working or gathering together on something shared, with the task visible.
direction.outdoor: Open country used for something — a track, a trail, a river — with the weather and the hour honest.
direction.luxury: Comfort placed in a landscape: a well-made room, terrace or camp with the view it was built for. Restrained, not glossy.
direction.eco-tourism: Conservation as work: a guide, a researcher, a ranger, or a trail crew doing the thing, with the habitat around them.
direction.photography: A view worth carrying a camera to, at the hour that makes it — the picture a photographer went there for.
direction.hidden-gems: Somewhere quiet and specific that is plainly not the famous view, and plainly worth the trip.
direction.why-visit: One frame that argues the case: something particular to this country happening in front of a landscape only this country has.

$comment_composition: Focal points in the country datasets are percentages. These turn them into words the model can act on, because a generated frame has no focal-point crop parameter — the composition has to be right in the original.

x: with the subject set to the left of centre
with the subject near the centre of the frame
with the subject set to the right of centre
y: and the interest high in the frame
and the horizon around the middle
and the interest low in the frame, with sky above
